page: Vultr voc-m-24c-192gb-4800s-amd is a memory-optimized cloud server belonging to the Optimized Cloud Compute family. It features 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical AMD EPYC cores operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Hardware multithreading provides two threads per physical core, supported by 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. Memory capacity is substantial at 192.0 GB of RAM, establishing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. Attached directly to the instance is 4800 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage, while accelerator hardware is omitted with zero GPUs.

Benchmark results highlight significant computational density and high-throughput memory channels. In raw compute tests, the server attained a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 69,533.1 and a PassMark CPU score of 51,801.15, positioning its parallel processing in the top 25% of evaluated hardware. Uncached memory performance is especially strong, registering 488.87 GB/sec in large-block read operations and 225.61 GB/sec in large-block writes, both placing in the top 10%. Application-level tests show mid-tier results, including 55.54 million Redis SET operations per second and a Geekbench multi-core score of 14,950.0.

Qualitatively, this instance provides cost efficiency for deployments demanding massive memory footprints and dense local storage on dedicated compute without paying for unused GPU silicon. Because the 4800 GB NVMe storage is bundled locally, it reduces dependencies on separate network-attached block volumes. The tradeoff lies in modest clock speeds and baseline per-thread performance, making it less optimal for workloads bound strictly by single-thread frequency.

This server type is engineered for heavy transactional databases, in-memory caches, distributed analytics nodes, data warehousing, and large ETL batch operations requiring vast memory overhead alongside fast local disk scratch space.
